description:
Hi! We are KaizenCode, a team passionate about technology, creativity, and solving problems. We believe technology can help us build a better future, not only for people but also for our planet. We are interested in developing innovative ideas to address environmental challenges and real-world problems.

Our team has experience with programming, web development, and AI tools. 

Let's work together to turn ideas into solutions for Earth and beyond!
summary:
We are taught when NASA reached the Moon, but never what it truly takes to survive there. For a child, space becomes just another date to memorize, not a world to explore.

STARBOUND was created to break that distance.

It is an interactive game that places young players inside a real mission. Instead of studying astronauts, they become one. Each challenge is based on authentic NASA work:

VEGGIE (ISS, 2014) - Learning to grow food with no soil.
Human Research Program - Understanding how space changes the body.
ARTEMIS - Preparing to land and live on the Moon.

Everyone has forgotten to water a plant. In space, that mistake could mean losing your only source of fresh food. Without learning to cultivate beyond Earth, living on another planet will never be possible.

Here, learning comes from decisions, not textbooks. When players must choose between producing oxygen or protecting their base from radiation, they finally understand what is truly at stake.

STARBOUND builds critical thinking, curiosity, and a genuine passion for science. It is not just a game. It is a first step toward the stars.
details:
STARBOUND: Junior Mission Control turns children into astronauts.

Instead of memorizing dates, players live a mission. They grow lettuce without soil, just as NASA did with VEGGIE on the ISS in 2014. They learn how space changes the human body, and they prepare for a lunar landing inspired by ARTEMIS. Every action has a consequence: if they forget to water a plant, they lose food. If they ignore radiation, they risk their base. If they waste oxygen, they risk everything.

That is its greatest benefit. Learning is no longer about reading and repeating. It is about deciding, failing, and understanding why. Children develop critical thinking, empathy for real astronauts, and a genuine curiosity for science, all while playing.

The project was built in Unity 6.0 LTS using C#, with visuals designed in Figma and Canva, audio edited in CapCut, and teamwork organized through GitHub and Visual Studio.

Its creativity lies in transforming survival into education. A simple choice becomes a lesson in biology, physics, and responsibility.

We considered age, accessibility, visual learning, and real NASA data, so any child, in any classroom, can feel what it means to reach for the stars.
dataRefs: Toolkit for educators and youth – Food production on the Moon and in remote areas
